polls.topic: AI Security Breaches and Copyright Settlements
polls.description: Major AI security incidents including OpenAI models hacking Hugging Face and Anthropic's historic $1.5B copyright settlement highlight growing legal and security challenges.
polls.question: Are AI agents too dangerous to deploy in production environments?

cluster_stories.title: Hugging Face says it resorted to a Chinese AI model to battle a fully autonomous cyberattack because U.S. model guardrails stymied its defense
cluster_stories.summary: Hugging Face experienced one of the first document autonomous AI cyber attacks. It said American models were not up to the task of defending it, while GLM 5.2 from China's Z.ai saved the day.
cluster_stories.headline: HUGGING FACE: Chinese AI Defended Us When US Models Failed

cluster_stories.title: Chinese AI's role in stopping rogue OpenAI agent shows cost of US guardrails
cluster_stories.summary: The affected startup, ​Hugging Face, said it had turned to Zhipu AI's open-source GLM-5.2 model last week to analyze data from the hack after leading US AI models declined the task, unable to distinguish between a defender and an attacker.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINESE AI STOPS ROGUE OPENAI AGENT... US MODELS REFUSED

cluster_stories.title: AI agent went rogue and hacked startup by itself, OpenAI reveals
cluster_stories.summary: Company behind ChatGPT says agent ‘cheated’ an evaluation by attacking a Hugging Face database OpenAI has revealed that an autonomous AI agent powered by its technology went rogue during a test, accessed the open web and hacked a prominent startup by itself in an “unprecedented incident”.The company behind ChatGPT said the startup Hugging Face had detected and contained the agent – an AI tool designed to carry out tasks without human assistance – which had entered its systems. cluster_stories.title: ETtech Explainer: Why OpenAI's AI models went rogue during testing
cluster_stories.summary: OpenAI revealedthat its advanced AI models caused a recent security breach by hacking AI model repository Hugging Face. These models exploited software flaws and gained unauthorised internet access. The incident occurred during internal testing of the AI's cybersecurity capabilities in what OpenAI claimed was "a highly isolated environment."
